main_body: Flat-roofed desert adobe house: a large sand-coloured roof terrace (rug, hatch, parapet rim) over a terracotta front wall with an arched wooden door and a lattice window
top_band: At x=32, light tan roof surface (L 175-202) from rows 1-31, with a lighter parapet edge at rows 28-31, then a dark eave row at 32-33. The roof carries a rug and a hatch, so it reads as a horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The scan shows a clear step from the light roof (L~175-202) to a dark eave line (L 70-96) and then the darker wall (L~122), which is a drop of about 50 L. The roof top is tall, but the rug and roof hatch on it make it a real horizontal surface, and a parapet lip closes it at the front. The wall below has crenel-like dark notches under the eave, and the door and window sit inside light frames with dark interiors. No isometric side face is drawn. It satisfies the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown, which is good. The wall and roof speckle and the rug add some texture, but the measured facts are well below the references. The candidate has 27 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 11% against 0% for both references. The door, window frame, rug interior and roof body are fairly flat blocks, and the surfaces lack the per-tile shading of the Beodeul stone and tile work. It looks thinner and flatter next to the references.
